A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COLIPRI research. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A-E support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, retrieval, report-generation, and segmentation experiments, together with extensive training ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds OSL comparisons, prompt-sensitivity experiments, a manual extraction audit, and MRI segmentation results.

M1.justification: The final COLIPRI architectures, CLIP/OSL/RRG/MAE objectives, sentence-pair construction algorithm, and inference procedures remain unchanged. The alternative sentence-pair schemes introduced in Appendix B.4 are experimental comparisons, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds segmentation on ACDC cardiac cine-MRI, MAMA-Mia breast DCE-MRI, and HNTS-MRG head-and-neck tumor MRI (Table D.4). This substantially expands evaluation beyond the earlier CT coverage to different modalities and anatomical regions. Existing datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Table B.8 adds evaluated alternatives to default OSL: naive sentence pairing and abnormality-label templates supervised on all 18 or the first nine classes. Main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. VocabFine receives new discussion but is not reported as a directly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 introduces all-class versus first-nine-class label supervision, separate evaluation of supervised and remaining classes, additional prompting conditions, and manual semantic checking of 50 extracted sentences from 20 sampled Findings texts. These add substantive controls and evaluation procedures; the retained benchmarks' splits, budgets, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds sentence-construction and class-generalization ablations, sensitivity tests for six alternative prompt templates, and an LLM extraction audit with two illustrative cases (Appendix B.4, Tables B.8-B.9). It also adds explicitly out-of-distribution MRI transfer tests in Table D.4.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 95% confidence intervals using 100 bootstrap samples for classification and 500 for report generation, plus fold-level segmentation reporting. The additions introduce no new seed disclosures, repeated-run reporting, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Retained result tables preserve their values, but v3 adds substantial new findings. Table B.8 reports last-nine-class AUPRC of 47.28 for default OSL versus 41.26 for first-nine label supervision. Table B.9 reports AUROC of 65.32 with Alt 2 versus 81.53 with default short prompts. New HNTS-MRG results at 37.5k steps are 65.15 DSC for COLIPRI-CRM versus 58.16 from scratch.

T1.justification: The OSL pair definitions, supervision labels, softmax probabilities, cross-entropy loss, and combined alignment objective in Appendix B.4, equations (1)-(7), are retained. No new theoretical result, proof, or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that OSL enables short-prompt classification and that combined multimodal and vision-only supervision produces versatile, state-of-the-art COLIPRI encoders. The revised abstract and contribution list emphasize existing ideas without changing their scientific scope or the main performance claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.4 adds explanations of shortcut learning in naive sentence pairing, limited transfer from closed-set supervision, sensitivity to negation wording, and missed findings during LLM extraction. Section 6 explicitly treats RRG as optional when retrieval is unimportant. Section 5.2 also adds a hypothesis that OSL could generalize beyond medical imaging.

D1.justification: v3 specifies how to construct the new sentence-pair controls, sample eight pairs with abnormality labels drawn without replacement, instantiate six evaluation prompt pairs, and manually check extraction fidelity. The original implementation settings, preprocessing prompts, model weights, and inference-code access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds a targeted distinction between OSL and CT-CLIP's closed-set VocabFine supervision. References add the three MRI datasets, BiomedCLIP, and Stock et al. on label-extraction reliability, while the PaLI citation is removed. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract and contribution list, sharpens several method headings, separates limitations from the conclusion, and adds author contributions and acknowledgements. Main-text and appendix references are separated. Most existing exposition and section order are preserved.

P2.justification: The document changes globally from two-column to single-column formatting. Figure 2 is rearranged into a 2-by-2 panel layout, Tables 4 and 5 are transposed, and existing displays are resized and relocated. Tables B.8, B.9, and D.4 add new displays.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports and qualifies OSL through controlled comparisons and prompt-sensitivity tests, while MRI experiments broaden the transfer evidence. Explicit discussion of extraction omissions and RRG's optional role improves practical interpretation. These strengthen an already extensively evaluated paper, although the extraction audit covers only 50 sentences without measuring recall, and MRI-specific implementation details remain sparse.
